question: US x Iran Effective Ceasefire by September 4?
research:
I finished the searches. Several direct page fetches (Polymarket, Wikipedia, CNN, Critical Threats, GlobalSecurity) were blocked by the proxy, so some details below come from search-result summaries and could not be checked against the full pages.

## 1. Resolution source
- The criteria give no URL. The market is Polymarket's "US x Iran Effective Ceasefire begins by...? (2 week pause)". It resolves on a "consensus of information" from its resolution sources. I could not load the page itself. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/us-x-iran-effective-ceasefire-begins-byptptpt-2-week-pause)
- I could not find when the September 4 contract was created. That date matters: if no qualifying strike happened after creation, the 14-day clock starts on the creation date.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The last US strike on Iranian land I could confirm was the wave on September 1, 2026.
- If that is the latest qualifying action, a clean 14-day period would start September 2 and finish at 12:00 PM ET on September 15. That is after today, so it is not complete.
- The big open question is whether the tanker strikes on September 5 and 8 count. The criteria exclude maritime territory and count only land and internal waters. Ships were hit "off" Kharg Island, "off" Jask, "near Kharg" and in the Gulf of Oman, which reads as at sea. If any of them were in Iranian internal waters or at a port berth, the clock would restart on that date. I found no source that pins down their legal location.

## 4. Base rates
- The pattern since the April ceasefire and the June memorandum of understanding is intermittent US strike waves with gaps between them: 7 May, about 9 June (Apache downing), about 7 July, late July, then a gap of roughly a month to August 30. [Wikipedia May 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7_May_2026_United_States_strikes_on_Iran); [CNBC Jun 9](https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/06/09/trump-iran-helicopter-hormuz-strait.html); [Al Jazeera Jul 7](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/7/us-says-strikes-launched-as-explosions-heard-in-southern-iran)
- 14-day gaps have happened often. A Polymarket "by August 12" contract reportedly resolved Yes, and a "by July 18" contract resolved No. [polyguana](https://polyguana.com/resolved/2937527); [coingape](https://coingape.com/prediction-markets/will-us-x-iran-have-an-effective-ceasefire-by-august-31/)
- Early September is a more intense phase. The US is now targeting Iran's economy through tanker strikes on top of a blockade in place since mid-April, and analysts describe a war of attrition. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/05/us-iran-oil-tankers-navy-missile-attack.html); [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/6/us-iran-engaged-in-tanker-war-where-is-the-months-long-conflict-headed)

## 5. Other forecasts
- Undated snapshot: the September 4 contract at 27¢, September 7 at 44¢ and September 30 at 75¢. I could not confirm when this was taken. [polym.trade](https://polym.trade/event/us-x-iran-effective-ceasefire-begins-byptptpt-2-week-pause)
- Earlier related contracts: "by August 31" traded around 51 to 53% at one point and around 95% at another. Sources are inconsistent on these. [CryptoRank](https://cryptorank.io/news/feed/ac8d6-polymarket-cuts-us-iran-ceasefire-odds-as-fresh-strike-risks-rattle-crypto-markets); [Blockonomi](https://blockonomi.com/us-iran-ceasefire-odds-drop-on-polymarket-this-week)
- I found no expert forecasts or Kalshi or Manifold equivalents.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (about September 18)
- 2026-09-15, 12:00 PM ET: the earliest a clean period could finish, assuming September 1 was the last qualifying strike. Any US air or missile strike on Iranian land or internal waters before then restarts the clock. A restart on September 5 or later would fall after the September 4 deadline.
- Ongoing triggers: Trump vowed on August 31 to hit Iran "hard." [Time](https://time.com/article/2026/08/31/us-iran-strikes-larak-island/) The IRGC has kept firing ballistic missiles at US warships, and CENTCOM said on September 8 this happened twice in two days. Iran keeps attacking US bases and shipping. Each of these could lead to new US strikes on coastal radars or launchers.
- Possible dispute over whether the tanker strikes near Kharg or Jask were inside Iranian internal waters. The rules allow up to 3 extra days when sources conflict.
- Diplomacy: Pakistani officials are reportedly mediating with Tehran (Al Jazeera live page, details unclear). Gulf states reportedly talked Washington out of resuming the war in early August. [GlobalSecurity](https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/ops/iran-war-20260906.htm)
